transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Lee. To start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I guess the main thing is people keep telling me I’m not listening. Like at work, my supervisor will be standing right there talking directly to me, explaining something, and I’m looking at him, I’m nodding, I’m not trying to be disrespectful or anything… but then a minute later I realize I only caught maybe half of what he said. And then I have to ask him to repeat it, which makes me look like I didn’t care or I was ignoring him.

It’s the same at home with my wife. She’ll tell me something, and I’ll think I’m listening, but then I miss parts of it and have to ask her again. It’s gotten to where people are frustrated with me, and honestly I’m frustrated too, because I’m not doing it on purpose. That’s really what brought me in.
Have you noticed any trouble actually hearing what people say—like needing the TV or phone volume louder, or missing words in noisy places—rather than just losing focus on the conversation?

I don’t think it’s my hearing, no. I mean, I haven’t really noticed needing the TV louder or anything like that. My wife doesn’t complain that I’ve got the volume blasting, and on the phone I can usually hear people fine.

It’s more like… I hear the sound of what they’re saying, but my brain doesn’t hang onto all of it. Like if there’s a lot going on around me, maybe I miss pieces, but it doesn’t feel like I can’t physically hear the words. It feels more like I kind of drift or I’m already thinking about the first part of what they said, and then I miss the next part. So, yeah, I don’t think it’s an ear problem, at least not that I’ve noticed.
Would you say this kind of difficulty focusing and missing parts of conversations has been present since you were a child or teenager, or is this something that's really only started recently?

Oh, no, this isn’t new. I mean, it’s definitely been more of a problem now because work and home stuff matter more, but I was like this way back as a kid.

I remember teachers moving my seat all the time, like putting me closer to them or away from certain kids, because I couldn’t just sit there and stay put. And I’d blurt things out, too—like if I knew an answer, I’d call it out before they finished asking, or before they called on me. I didn’t always mean to be rude, I just… the answer would be there and it would come out.

And I got in trouble for butting into other kids’ work. Like before middle school, I’d lean over or jump into what someone else was doing, try to help or comment or tell them what I thought, and the teacher would get on me for not minding my own paper. So yeah, looking back, it’s been there a long time. It wasn’t something that just started recently.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports chronic, pervasive inattention (missing parts of conversations at work and home, drifting attention) confirmed to be present since childhood, along with childhood history of hyperactive-impulsive symptoms (frequent seat changes by teachers, inability to stay seated, blurting out answers, interrupting/intruding on others' work).
